subject: Biology
title: Neural Control and Coordination
summary: The nervous system is made of neurons that carry electrical impulses. The human system has the central nervous system (brain and spinal cord) and the peripheral nervous system (cranial and spinal nerves; somatic and autonomic).
A resting neuron is polarised (outside positive, inside negative, about −70 mV) because of the Na⁺/K⁺ pump. A stimulus opens Na⁺ channels, giving an action potential that travels along the axon.
Impulses pass to the next cell across synapses — electrical (fast) or chemical (neurotransmitters such as acetylcholine).
The brain has forebrain (cerebrum, thalamus, hypothalamus), midbrain and hindbrain (pons, cerebellum, medulla); the medulla and pons form part of the brain stem.

formulas.name: Neuron parts
formulas.formula: cell body (cyton, with Nissl's granules) + dendrites (carry impulses towards cell body) + axon (carries impulses away, ends in synaptic knobs)

formulas.name: Myelinated vs non-myelinated
formulas.formula: myelinated: Schwann cells form myelin sheath, nodes of Ranvier — spinal and cranial nerves (saltatory, faster conduction);  non-myelinated: autonomous and somatic neural systems

formulas.name: Resting potential
formulas.formula: inside −ve, outside +ve;  high K⁺ and negative proteins inside, high Na⁺ outside;  Na⁺/K⁺ pump: 3 Na⁺ out, 2 K⁺ in per ATP

formulas.name: Action potential
formulas.formula: stimulus → Na⁺ channels open → Na⁺ rushes in → depolarisation (inside +ve);  then K⁺ channels open → K⁺ moves out → repolarisation

formulas.name: Synapse types
formulas.formula: electrical (gap junctions, very fast, rare);  chemical (synaptic cleft; neurotransmitter like acetylcholine released from vesicles binds receptors on post-synaptic membrane)

formulas.name: Forebrain
formulas.formula: cerebrum (two hemispheres joined by corpus callosum; cortex = grey matter, sensory, motor and association areas);  thalamus (relay centre);  hypothalamus (body temperature, hunger, thirst, neurosecretory cells → hormones)
formulas.when: Parts and functions of the forebrain.

formulas.name: Limbic system
formulas.formula: amygdala + hippocampus + inner parts of cerebral hemispheres + hypothalamus → sexual behaviour, emotional reactions (excitement, pleasure, rage, fear) and motivation

formulas.name: Midbrain
formulas.formula: corpora quadrigemina (four lobes) — visual and auditory reflexes; cerebral aqueduct passes through

formulas.name: Hindbrain
formulas.formula: pons (connects brain regions, respiratory centre);  cerebellum (balance, posture, coordination; 'little brain' with many folds);  medulla oblongata (respiration, cardiovascular reflexes, gastric secretions)
formulas.note: Brain stem = midbrain + pons + medulla oblongata.

formulas.name: Reflex arc
formulas.formula: receptor → afferent (sensory) neuron → spinal cord (inter-neuron) → efferent (motor) neuron → effector

formulas.name: Eye layers
formulas.formula: sclera (outer, cornea in front) → choroid (middle, iris, ciliary body) → retina (inner: ganglion cells, bipolar cells, photoreceptors — rods and cones)

formulas.name: Photoreceptors
formulas.formula: rods: rhodopsin (visual purple), dim light (scotopic) vision;  cones: photopsins, bright light (photopic) and colour vision (red, green, blue)
formulas.note: Fovea has only cones (sharpest vision); blind spot has no photoreceptors.

formulas.name: Ear parts and functions
formulas.formula: outer: pinna, auditory canal, tympanic membrane;  middle: malleus, incus, stapes (ossicles), Eustachian tube;  inner: cochlea (hearing — organ of Corti on basilar membrane), vestibular apparatus (balance — crista in ampullae, macula in saccule and utricle)

examples.title: Sensory or motor?
examples.problem: Which neurons carry impulses from the spinal cord to muscles?
examples.solution: Efferent (motor) neurons. Afferent (sensory) neurons carry impulses from receptors to the CNS.

examples.title: Depolarisation
examples.problem: Which ion movement causes the rising phase of an action potential?
examples.solution: Rapid influx of Na⁺ through voltage-gated sodium channels reverses the polarity (inside becomes positive).

examples.title: Function of hypothalamus
examples.problem: Name three functions controlled by the hypothalamus.
examples.solution: Body temperature, hunger and thirst (urge for eating and drinking); it also has neurosecretory cells making hypothalamic hormones.

examples.title: Blind spot
examples.problem: Why can't we see an image falling on the blind spot?
examples.solution: At the blind spot the optic nerve leaves the eye and retinal blood vessels enter; there are no photoreceptor cells.

examples.title: Saltatory conduction
examples.problem: Why is conduction faster in myelinated fibres?
examples.solution: Myelin insulates the axon; impulses jump from one node of Ranvier to the next (saltatory conduction).

examples.title: Hearing mechanism
examples.problem: Trace the path of sound to the brain.
examples.solution: Pinna → ear canal → tympanic membrane vibrates → ossicles (malleus, incus, stapes) → oval window → waves in cochlear lymph → basilar membrane moves → hair cells of organ of Corti bend → nerve impulses via auditory nerve → auditory cortex.

topics.title: Neural system in animals
topics.explain: Lower invertebrates have a simple network of neurons (Hydra — nerve net). Insects have a brain and many ganglia. Vertebrates have a more developed system.

topics.title: Autonomic nervous system
topics.explain: Part of the PNS controlling involuntary organs and smooth muscles; divided into sympathetic and parasympathetic systems, which usually have opposite effects.

topics.title: Human brain coverings
topics.explain: The brain is protected by the skull and three meninges: outer dura mater, thin middle arachnoid and inner pia mater (in contact with brain tissue). Cerebrospinal fluid cushions it.

topics.title: Cerebral cortex
topics.explain: Grey matter (cell bodies) on the outside with convolutions; white matter (myelinated tracts) inside. Association areas handle complex functions such as intersensory associations, memory and communication.

topics.title: Image formation
topics.explain: Light passes through cornea and lens and forms an image on the retina. Light changes retinal (a vitamin A derivative) in rhodopsin, generating potentials in photoreceptors that pass via bipolar and ganglion cells to the optic nerve and visual cortex.

topics.title: Sensory organs other than eye and ear
topics.explain: Nose has olfactory receptors (olfactory epithelium connects to the limbic system); tongue has taste buds; skin has touch, pressure, pain and temperature receptors.

ratta: Resting potential: inside −ve; Na⁺/K⁺ pump 3 out, 2 in.
Depolarisation = Na⁺ in;  repolarisation = K⁺ out.
Multipolar cortex;  bipolar retina;  unipolar embryo.
Thalamus relay;  hypothalamus temperature, hunger, thirst.
Cerebellum balance;  medulla breathing & heart reflexes.
